rationale: Both correctly use the Rational Root Theorem to list the candidates ±1 and ±1/2. A goes further and shows that each candidate actually occurs for some integer coefficients. Its examples a3=-3, 3, -9, 9 (with the other coefficients 0) all check out. This matters because the question asks for 'possible' rational roots, and the theorem alone only gives an upper bound. B stops at the candidate list, so it leaves the realizability step unjustified.
